title: Tool-proxy adaptor and lazy client surface — PRD sketch
content:
Context

We frequently see customers building client-side integrations that need to: run long-running tool calls (search, database queries, multi-step webhooks), receive partial progress, and optionally hydrate full tool responses later. Current hosted-api streaming covers model tokens and action frames but puts responsibility for orchestration and resume semantics on clients. This PRD sketch proposes a lightweight middle layer: a Tool-Proxy Adaptor + Lazy Client Surface that sits between the Hosted API streaming protocol and customer SDKs.

Goals
- Provide a consistent, low-friction contract for incremental tool results that:
  - lets clients show early progress (summary, status, partial artifacts)
  - enables safe resume/replay after network disconnects or client restarts
  - minimizes bandwidth by supporting shallow frames and on-demand hydration
- Improve developer ergonomics in SDKs (JS/TS, Python, mobile) with small surface area additions
- Keep server-side complexity bounded: adaptor should be optional and composable with current tool-calling primitives

Non-goals
- Not replacing full orchestration (no attempt to become a workflow engine)
- Not enforcing a single tool RPC transport (we will support HTTP/webhook and gRPC backends but not provide built-in adapters for every third-party API)

User stories
- Frontend engineer (mobile): "I want my chat UI to show 'indexing db...' with a spinner and then show the final results when available, even if the user loses connectivity."
- Platform engineer: "I want a predictable format for tool events so I can build observability and cost accounting without custom parsing across teams."
- SDK consumer: "I don't want to pull down a dozen fields; give me a tiny object for progress and a handle I can call to hydrate full output later."

Design sketch
1) Data model (flat envelope)
We introduce compact, top-level envelopes inside streaming frames and final response payloads. Envelope fields (all strings / lists):
- session_id: short opaque id (uuid-v4-ish)
- checkpoint_id: stable id for a session snapshot (client-visible)
- tool_handle: opaque handle used for on-demand hydration (short token)
- phase: enum (START, PROGRESS, PARTIAL_OUTPUT, FINAL_OUTPUT, ERROR)
- summary: short text summary for UI (optional)
- size_hint: approximate bytes or units for full payload (optional)
- checksum: sha256 hex of full payload (optional)
- artifacts: list of tiny metadata objects (represented as JSON-encoded strings)

Rationale: keep envelope flat and string-typed to make it easy to pass through existing loggers and telemetry. We intentionally avoid embedding large nested JSONs in progress frames.

2) Two-layer streaming model
- Shallow frames: frequent, cheap; contain session_id, checkpoint_id, phase=PROGRESS, summary, artifacts list (metadata only).
- Hydration API: separate HTTP endpoint to fetch full tool output using tool_handle and optional checkpoint_id. Returns structured JSON for tool output in one request or as a small (non-infinite) stream.

3) Example flow (ASCII sequence)
Client -> Hosted API (model call w/ tool binding) : start stream
Hosted API -> Client : streaming frames (tokens + envelope {session_id, checkpoint_id=1, phase=START})
Tool backend -> Hosted API : starts executing; emits PROGRESS frames with summaries (checkpoint_id increments)
Client loses connectivity / UI closed
Later: Client calls Hydration: GET /v1/tool-hydrate?handle=<tool_handle>&checkpoint=<checkpoint_id>
Server -> Client : returns final structured output (or 202 if still processing)

4) Tool-handle semantics
- Generated by Hosted API when tool call is initiated; short-lived by default (24h) but configurable for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Statelessly referenceable: includes enough metadata to route to the right tool-adaptor instance (no direct secrets).
- Hydration requests require API key with the same permissions as the originating model call.

SDK ergonomics proposals
Pattern A — Lazy consumption (default) - JS/TS: stream() returns an async iterator of {deltaTokens?, envelope?}
    for await (const frame of client.stream(req)) {
      if (frame.envelope && frame.envelope.phase === 'PROGRESS') {
        renderProgress(frame.envelope.summary)
      }
      appendTokens(frame.deltaTokens)
    }
- Hydrate helper: client.hydrateTool(handle, {checkpoint_id}) -> Promise<FullToolOutput>

Pattern B — Auto-hydrate (opt-in)
- client.stream(req, {autoHydrate: true, parallelHydrate: 2}) will automatically call hydrate when it sees FINAL_OUTPUT phase and attach full tool outputs to the stream frames. Useful for server-side where you want one consolidated response.

Pattern C — Attach-on-demand (mobile)
- SDKs expose a small model-binding object: {sessionId, latestCheckpoint, getPreview(), hydrate()}. The UI can show getPreview() result synchronously and call hydrate() on tap.

Observability and telemetry
- Emit structured logs for: session_start, checkpoint_emit, hydrate_request, hydrate_result, checksum_mismatch, hydrate_timeout.
- Metric KPIs: average time to first PROGRESS (target < 400ms), hydration request success rate (> 99.5%), median hydration latency (SLO 200ms for cached / warm results, 1.5s for cold), % of streams that use hydration (we expect ~20% for early adopters).
- Billing: hydration calls are billable (token/compute units); provide tooling to attribute cost to originating model call.

Compatibility with existing features
- Tool-Proxy Adaptor is an optional layer on top of current tool-calling interface. If not enabled, behavior is unchanged.
- Existing streaming SDKs will get envelope fields as extras inside event frames; minimal breakage by design.

Security and privacy
- Tool handles must never contain PII in the raw string.
- Hydration endpoint enforces same-origin permissions: only the same project/org key that initiated the tool call can hydrate (unless explicit cross-project sharing).
- Checkpoint ids are ephemeral and cannot be used to escalate access.

Operational considerations
- Adaptor will keep short-lived checkpoints in fast store (Redis) and persist final outputs to S3 (or customer-specified object store for Private).
- To minimize storage, we keep only metadata for non-final checkpoints and garbage-collect after configurable TTL.

Migration and rollout plan
Phase 0 (experimentation) — feature flag behind dev teams (2 weeks)
- Implement adaptor in hosted-infra sandbox; expose envelope fields in streaming responses.
- SDK prototypes (JS/TS, Python) with lazy-hydrate helpers.
- Observe telemetry, collect feedback from 3 PD teams.

Phase 1 (beta) — 8 weeks
- Public beta enabled for new customers and opt-in for existing.
- Docs + cheap migrations guide.
- Implement hydration billing attribution.

Phase 2 (GA) — 12–16 weeks after beta
- Backwards-compatible default behavior; full docs; migration checklist.
- Add config to Dedicated/Private for longer handle lifetimes and S3 routing.

Open questions / trade-offs
- Pricing model: should hydration be charged at full model token rates or a lower tier? (Finance prefers separate tier)
- Checkpoint frequency: who decides? Model heuristics vs. explicit developer frames.
- Do we need a streaming hydration mode (server pushes hydration results to client) vs polling GET? (push complicates auth and firewalls)
- Error semantics: how to surface partial tool failure vs model failure consistently?

Implementation notes (engineering hints)
- Reuse existing streaming frame schema; add an "envelope_v2" micro-format to avoid breaking older SDKs.
- Tool adaptor should be implemented as a small library with a clear interface: startToolCall(binding, metadata) -> {tool_handle, initial_checkpoint}
- Hydration endpoint: GET /v1/tool-hydrate?handle={}&checkpoint={}&prefer=full|summary
- Back-pressure: enforce limits on concurrent hydrations per org (default 20)

Checklist / next steps
- [ ] RFC for envelope_v2 and tool_handle encoding (security review) — assigned Samir (due 2025-01-24)
- [ ] Prototype hydrating helper in JS SDK (Avery) — due 2025-01-31
- [ ] Telemetry event spec and dashboards (Monica) — due 2025-02-07
- [ ] Billing impact analysis and pricing proposal (Finance sync) — scheduled 2025-02-10

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- Could combine with cached prefix/KV to hydrate using a delta approach (send only missing chunks). Keep for later.
- Mobile UX: consider an out-of-band push notification for big final outputs so app can fetch on demand.
- Explore making compact artifact metadata an arrow-parquet pointer for large binary results.

References
- Related: incremental-deferred-tool-invocation-and-sdk-hydration-notes (drive)
- Observability playbooks: streaming-tool-handshake-observability-checklist

End of sketch — feedback welcome.

Unresolved: consolidate naming (checkpoint vs snapshot vs frame_id) before Beta.
